title: Constructions
prerequisites: Similarity of triangles and the ratio of sides.

topics.title: Division of a Segment and Similar Triangles
topics.quick_summary: A line segment can be divided in any given ratio using a ray of equally spaced points, and the same idea constructs a triangle similar to a given one in a required scale factor.
topics.real_life: An architect scaling a plan to two-thirds size uses exactly this construction rather than recomputing every measurement.

detailed.definition: To divide a segment AB in the ratio m : n, draw an acute-angled ray from A, mark m + n equal arcs along it, join the last point to B, and draw a parallel through the mth point.
detailed.key_idea: The construction works by the Basic Proportionality Theorem — the parallel line divides AB in the same ratio as the ray was divided. Every step has a justification.
detailed.working_principle: For a similar triangle with scale factor m/n, mark the larger of m and n arcs along the ray. Getting this choice right is what decides whether the new triangle is larger or smaller.
applications: Scale factor greater than 1 gives a larger triangle; less than 1 gives a smaller one.
The arcs on the ray must be exactly equal, so the compass width must not change.
The justification is expected in the answer, not only the drawing.

points: Mark m + n equal arcs when dividing a segment in the ratio m : n.
The construction is justified by the Basic Proportionality Theorem.
For a scale factor m/n, use the greater of m and n as the number of arcs.
Keep the compass width unchanged while marking equal arcs.
Write the steps of construction and the justification; both carry marks.
mistakes: Marking m arcs instead of m + n when dividing in the ratio m : n.
Changing the compass width partway through marking the arcs.
Omitting the justification, which is separately marked.
topics.memory_hook: 'm + n equal arcs, then one parallel line' — the ratio transfers automatically.
topics.advanced: This is a constructive proof of the Basic Proportionality Theorem. The same principle underlies the slide rule and every mechanical scaling device built before calculators.

topics.title: Construction of Tangents to a Circle
topics.quick_summary: Tangents from an external point are constructed by drawing a circle on the line joining the point to the centre as diameter, and joining the intersections.
topics.real_life: Marking where a belt leaves a pulley when it runs to a fixed post is exactly this construction on a workshop floor.

detailed.definition: To construct tangents from an external point P to a circle with centre O, find the mid-point M of OP, draw a circle with centre M and radius MO, and join P to the two points where the circles intersect.
detailed.key_idea: The construction works because an angle in a semicircle is a right angle. The circle on OP as diameter forces OA ⟂ PA, which is exactly the tangent condition.
detailed.working_principle: When the centre is not marked, it is first located by drawing two chords and their perpendicular bisectors, which meet at the centre.
applications: Two tangents can be drawn from any external point.
Only one tangent exists at a point on the circle itself.
The tangent lengths from P are equal, which serves as a check on the drawing.

points: Find the mid-point of OP and draw a circle with OP as diameter.
The intersections of the two circles are the points of contact.
Justification: angle in a semicircle is 90°, so the radius is perpendicular to the tangent.
If the centre is not given, locate it using the perpendicular bisectors of two chords.
Check the drawing by verifying that the two tangent lengths are equal.
mistakes: Taking the mid-point of the radius instead of OP.
Drawing tangents by eye rather than by construction.
Omitting the justification based on the angle in a semicircle.
topics.memory_hook: 'Circle on OP as diameter' — the semicircle supplies the right angle for free.
topics.advanced: The construction is the geometric solution of a quadratic: the two intersection points correspond to the two roots. Where the external point lies on the circle, the roots coincide and only one tangent exists.
